tasks.short: Check tools, climbing gear and insulated gloves, record the checks, hold the pre-job safety briefing, erect barriers and signs around the work area, and complete the job safety checklist.

steps.what: Line worker checks tools, climbing gear and insulated gloves before work
Line worker records equipment checks and test dates: on a paper inspection card today; after the change the scan shows the test date and the worker records the check
Line worker holds the pre-job safety briefing with the crew
Line worker adheres to safety procedures by erecting barriers and signs around work areas
Line worker fills in the job safety checklist and signs it: on paper today, in the work order with location and hazards filled in after the change

tasks.design: Each piece of safety gear carries a barcode; scanning it in the mobile work order ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows its last test date and flags gear that is overdue, so test dates are no longer copied onto a card; the worker still records each check. The job safety checklist is a form in the same work order, with the job's location and hazards filled in. Checking gear by hand, the safety briefing and putting up barriers stay with the crew; check records are kept per piece of gear, not used to rate workers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment checks and safety checklists lived on paper cards in the van.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders scan asset barcodes and host safety checklists.
tasks.still_hard: A tick on a form does not prove the check was done properly.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a nick in an insulated glove before it fails.

reach.learn: Whether overdue gear is taken out of use sooner.

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM keeps preventive maintenance plans and repair history and offers barcode fault reporting for technicians.
Work orders with time stamps or locations can observe technicians, so the works council must consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the crew's equipment to the signed safety checklist; the repair work itself is outside.
Input contract: gear test dates kept by the tool store; job hazards from the planner; fallback is paper cards.

Checking gear, briefing and barriers keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because only copying test dates goes and recording the check stays; s5 keeps 80 because location and hazards fill in and the crew still works through and signs the checklist.
unknowns: Pieces of safety gear per crew.
research_questions: Is overdue gear found before use more often?

incremental.description: Line worker reports damaged barcodes to the tool store.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many barcodes are damaged or missing outdoors, so most test dates are still copied and hazards written (1.5); high: gear barcoded and hazards from the planner (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive the day's work orders, agree tasks with the crew, coordinate switching with the control room, arrange materials with the warehouse, report the job complete and send the completion report to planning.

steps.what: Line worker receives the day's work orders from the planner on paper or by phone
Line worker coordinates work assignment preparation with the crew at the start of the day
Line worker coordinates switching and outages with the control room by phone
Line worker arranges materials and vehicles with the warehouse by phone
Line worker writes up completion of the assignment with hours and materials used: on paper today; in the app with fault and cause codes, hours and the material list to confirm after the change
Line worker checks the final completion report: work done, codes, hours and materials used
Line worker sends the checked completion report to the planner: handed over on paper today, sent from the app after the change

tasks.design: Work orders arrive in the crew's mobile work order app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with location, drawings and a material list that the warehouse picks from, so fewer calls are needed. On completion the worker picks fault and cause codes, enters hours and confirms the materials used; the worker checks the final report and sends it once to planning, which passes it on to finance. Agreeing tasks with the crew and coordinating switching with the control room stay by voice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders came on paper or by phone, and completion was written up and re-keyed by the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders carry material lists and completion forms linked to planning and finance.
tasks.still_hard: Storm work changes plans faster than any system updates.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing who climbs and who stays on the ground on a hard job.

reach.learn: Whether completion data arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: At Altitude Infra, Praxedo mobile work orders saved about 8 hours per technician per week on work-order mail, entry and reports; period not stated, vendor case.
Work orders with time stamps or locations can observe technicians, so the works council must consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from planned jobs to the report with planning; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: jobs from the planner; switching orders from the control room by voice; fallback is paper and phone.

Coordinating with the crew and the control room and the report check keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for reading the work order; s4 keeps 50 for calls about missing items; s5 keeps 75 because only writing out the materials goes; s6 keeps 20 for the send.
Work order times are used for planning, not to rate workers.
research_questions: Do calls to the warehouse fall?

incremental.description: Line worker corrects material lists that do not match the job.

approvals.approved_version: The completion report with work done, codes, hours and materials exactly as checked by the worker in s5c, sent once to planning, which passes it on to finance; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly storm and fault work with changing plans, so jobs and materials are still arranged by phone (11.2); high: mostly planned jobs with known materials (22.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The line worker keeps safety checks, barriers, crew coordination and switching by voice; paper cards, phone calls for orders and materials, and written completion reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A crew that starts work sooner because everything is ready.
